metaDescription: Own mineral rights near El Paso, Arkansas, a small White County community? We evaluate legacy Fayetteville Shale interests here and make a no-obligation cash offer.
heroLead: El Paso is a small unincorporated community in White County, and mineral ownership here is almost always inherited land nobody has actively managed.
intro: There isn't much of a commercial center here, which is typical for this part of White County, but the surrounding sections were included in Fayetteville Shale leasing during the boom years like most of the rest of the county. If you hold an interest near El Paso, it likely came down through family land rather than a deal you made yourself, and it may be years since anyone checked on its current status.

sections.heading: A quiet corner of the Fayetteville Shale's eastern flank
paragraphs: Like the rest of eastern White County, well results around El Paso were generally modest compared to the play's core. Some tracts here were drilled and produced for a period before declining; others were leased but never developed at all. We check your specific section's history before quoting.

sections.heading: Reconstructing ownership on older family interests
paragraphs: It's common for interests in this area to have passed down through a family without a formal partition, meaning several relatives may each hold an undivided fraction. We can usually work from a deed, an old lease, or even just a family name to trace ownership through White County records rather than requiring you to have everything organized in advance.
If your interest turns out to be small, that's fine, we buy fractional interests of all sizes and price based on what's actually there.

sections.heading: What to expect if a well was never drilled on your tract
paragraphs: An interest with no drilling history is valued differently than a producing royalty. We're upfront about which situation applies before making an offer.

faqs.question: How do I know if a well was ever drilled on our family's land near El Paso?
faqs.answer: Send us your legal description or deed and we'll check operator and permit records for that specific tract.

faqs.question: Several relatives share ownership of the same interest. Can you handle that?
faqs.answer: Yes, we regularly work with multiple heirs on a single interest and can structure the purchase to account for each person's share.

faqs.question: Is our small interest even worth pursuing?
faqs.answer: Often yes. Small interests are common in this area, and we evaluate them individually rather than assuming a minimum size is required.

faqs.question: How long does a typical purchase take once we agree on a price?
faqs.answer: Once title is confirmed clean, closing on a straightforward El Paso-area interest usually takes a few weeks, longer only if a title issue needs resolving first.
